title: Review of phase_membrane repair with branched same-seed twins (seeds 7, 8): wall and ring always regrow, size recovery 2 of 4
summary: Ran phase_membrane unchanged with labkit's rim damage (120:0.5:rim) on seed 7, and a branched-twin test (twin_repair.py): at t=6000 two isolated, round (aspect 1.13-1.23), median-sized cells per seed lose 36-38% of their area to a bath disk centred on the wall; the damaged copy and an exact undamaged copy run to t=7600 and the same cell is followed in both. In all 4 cuts the wall closes and the link ring returns to the twin's level within 200-400 t (rim/core 1.55-1.68 right after the cut -> 1.85-1.95, twin 1.88-2.06). On seed 7 both cells reach 0.90-0.99 of the twin's area by +200-400 t. On seed 8 both cut cells first shrink to 22-25% of the twin (72 px) before regrowing, and later comparisons are confounded by the twins dividing. labkit's damage.png on seed 7: the cut cell (25% lost) closes by t=6250 and keeps growing.

observations.B: twin_s7.txt / twin_s8.txt: L rim/core 1.8-2.1 in undamaged cells; rerun/seed7/radial.png
observations.R: twin_s7.txt: cells 17 and 6 (37% erased) at 0.90-0.99 of their undamaged twin by t=6200-6400 with ring restored; rerun/seed7/damage.png t=6250

seeds_run.result: pass (2/2 cuts recover area and ring)
partial (ring recovers, area falls to 0.22-0.25 of twin before regrowing)

controls_run.R: twin_s7.txt, twin_s8.txt: exact undamaged copies of the state at t=6000 (branched twins), same cells followed

verdicts.limitation: Repair is curvature flow plus the link tilt, i.e. automatic by construction. Cells grow continuously (twin area 159 -> 636 in 1200 t) and divide, so 'mature' is ill-defined and area ratios after ~+800 t compare a dividing twin with a delayed one. On seed 8 the cut cells lost most of their remaining area (possibly splitting off a piece) before regrowing; my follower takes the largest overlapping piece. 4 cuts on 2 seeds, one fraction (~0.37).
